title: fix: replace dead Z-Image Vast GPU after host-reclaim outage
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
## What happened

Production Z-Image instance `46003779` (RTX 5090, California, $0.351/hr) went down around 2026-09-14 03:26 UTC. The host lost the container, and by the time it was caught the host had reclaimed the GPU slot entirely — `vastai start` returned "Required resources are currently unavailable" and the same machine showed up as a fresh offer to other renters. Not recoverable.

For roughly two days, all Z-Image traffic ran on the Fal fallback. No user-facing errors (100% success, 0 5xx per the monitor), but zero Vast redundancy and full fallback pricing instead of the Vast rate. The dead instance kept billing storage-only (~$0.044/hr) the whole time.

## What changed

- Rented and validated a replacement (`51212460`, RTX 5090, South Korea, $0.622/hr, reliability 0.9985) in isolation: auth rejection (403), 512x512/1024x1024 generation, oversized-dimension rejection (422), byte-identical fixed-seed output, `QUEUE_LIMIT=3` burst shedding (3 admitted, 4th shed in 20ms), restart recovery (~10s once weights cached).
- Joined it to the existing shared Cloudflare Tunnel (`zimage-vast.myceli.ai`) using the tunnel's existing connector token — no new tunnel or secret created. All four QUIC connections registered, worker appeared in `/register`, 9/9 attributed production requests returned 200.
- Destroyed the dead `46003779` instance.
- Updated `GPU_INSTANCES.md` with the new instance, rate, and incident notes.

## Note on price

New rate ($0.622/hr) is higher than the old one ($0.351/hr) because live RTX 5090 offers meeting our verified/reliability/bandwidth bar were running ~$0.54–0.66/hr at rental time — the old rate was a deal from whenever that instance was originally provisioned, not current market. This is a placeholder; a cheaper replacement is a planned follow-up.

gist.blurb: A reclaimed GPU left its old flowerpot, so Polli found Z-Image a fresh RTX 5090 home and plugged it back into the shared tunnel. The fallback kept the lights on; redundancy is back where it belongs.
gist.summary: Replaced the unrecoverable Vast Z-Image instance 46003779 with validated RTX 5090 instance 51212460, reconnecting it through the existing zimage-vast.myceli.ai Cloudflare Tunnel and restoring Vast-backed generation redundancy.
gist.impact: Z-Image requests continue returning successfully with a tested Vast backend alongside the Fal fallback, including verified fixed-seed output, dimension validation, burst shedding, and restart recovery.
